checkpoints.description: [2/3]-[3/3] Delivered MCP boundary validation: params are preserved (empty list no longer becomes {}), resources/read and prompts/get reject non-object params with -32602, tools/call rejects non-object arguments, and public dispatch_tool raises LatticeError for non-dict arguments. open_database validates path type and emptiness before Path/sqlite. ADR-017/README document WAL and allowlist caveats. checklists: passed; 173/173 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates. Uncommitted by PRINCIPLE-018 R1.
Task 'lattice-protocol-params-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Failing-first tests: client.call_tool and dispatch_tool reject non-string tool names, and LatticeClient/open_database normalize a whitespace-wrapped :memory: sentinel while preserving real paths. [2/3] Add name guards and align client/database path normalization. [3/3] Refresh the map, run gates and complete.

impact_assessment.why: Verification found two low API inconsistencies: an unhashable tool name crashes only the read-only allowlist check, and LatticeClient strips path whitespace while open_database preserves it.
impact_assessment.benefits: Both entry points reject malformed names with the Error/Why/Fix triad, and a database path opens the same way through the client and the database layer, including a whitespace-wrapped :memory: sentinel.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: non-string tool names now fail consistently; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: path handling changes only for whitespace around the sentinel and for previously stripped real paths.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate names before any set membership or dispatch, normalize only the :memory: sentinel in one shared style, preserve other path text, and pin both behaviors with client, MCP and database tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3]-[3/3] Added string-name guards to LatticeClient.call_tool and public dispatch_tool, made tools/call reject blank names with -32602, and normalized a whitespace-wrapped :memory: sentinel in both LatticeClient and open_database while preserving real path text. checklists: passed; 177/177 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates. Uncommitted by PRINCIPLE-018 R1.
Task 'lattice-api-consistency-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: add graph snapshot diffing - a lattice/diff.py module comparing two JSONL snapshots or a snapshot against the live repository, a diff CLI command, api.py re-exports, failing-first tests and README docs

impact_assessment.why: snapshots can be exported and imported but never compared; users and agents cannot see how an evidence graph evolved between two points in time
impact_assessment.benefits: a deterministic added/removed/changed report across papers, questions, claims and edges, usable from CLI, Python API and scripts via exit code
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new public functions diff_records/diff_snapshots/diff_snapshot and read_snapshot_records/collect_repository_records in snapshots.py; dependency: none, stdlib only; concurrency: read-only comparison, no writes; state: comparison ignores the volatile created_at field
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for all three entry points and the created_at rule, refactor export/import onto the shared record collectors with the existing snapshot roundtrip test as the guard, and run the full Phase 4 gate via aikit check

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Delivered deterministic snapshot diffing: lattice/diff.py (diff_records, diff_snapshots, diff_snapshot), shared record readers in snapshots.py, diff CLI command with git-style exit code, read-only diff_snapshot MCP tool with client methods, api re-exports, 11 new tests (189 total pass), README and ADR-019; 4/4 gates pass (test, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); checklists: passed; commit is blocked pending user authorization
Task 'lattice-snapshot-diff-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: integrate the AIKit UI mechanics - a tools/ui_inventory.py snapshot proof over the Research Studio (element ids, click handlers, roles, live regions, theme tokens, dispatcher routes), a committed .aikit/ui.json contract bounding the studio surface to lattice/web.py with protected paths, fast proof and diff limits, failing-first tests, README docs and an ADR

impact_assessment.why: lattice serves a large single-file web studio but has no UI contract, so aikit ui begin/verify/finish cannot bound or prove surface edits
impact_assessment.benefits: studio edits become bounded tasks with inventory, budget and style proofs; a dropped control, route or theme token becomes a verify finding instead of silent regressions
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new .aikit/ui.json (schema 1) plus tools package; dependency: none, stdlib only, pure parsing with no server start; concurrency: read-only inventory, no writes; state: ui.json must be committed before any ui begin, and an open ui task blocks delivery
impact_assessment.mitigation: mirror fold's proven inventory-tool and contract pattern, assert real studio entries in failing-first tests, validate the contract through load_contract, and keep the surface a single bounded file

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Integrated the AIKit UI mechanics: committed-ready .aikit/ui.json contract bounding the studio surface to lattice/web.py with 29 protected paths, tools/ui_inventory.py snapshot proof (116 entries: element ids, click handlers, roles, live regions, GET/POST routes, theme tokens; pure parsing, imports the exact served WEB_HTML), tests/test_ui_inventory.py, README docs and ADR-020; contract validated through load_contract; 4/4 gates pass (test 191, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); checklists: passed; the contract itself still needs a commit before ui begin can open a task
Task 'lattice-ui-guard-v1' completed successfully.

[1/5] Plan: validation and adoption pass - (2) a pointed .pdf ingestion guard with documented conversion recipes, (3) a PRINCIPLE-015 dogfood gate driving the real CLI golden path and the live studio server over HTTP plus chaos perturbations, (4) an agent integration guide for the MCP channel, (5) evidence-health metrics (claims per paper, answered questions, contradiction pairs, coverage gaps) in stats

impact_assessment.why: the PM diagnosis: engineering quality is high but adoption friction is unmeasured - PDF input is a wall, the golden path is never exercised end-to-end as a gate, the agent channel is undocumented, and success metrics do not exist
impact_assessment.benefits: lower input friction with a tested recipe path, a repeatable real-usage gate that catches workflow regressions, a documented MCP integration story, and measurable evidence health from any graph
impact_assessment.risks: contract: parse_file gains a .pdf branch, repository.stats gains an evidence block (machine consumers must tolerate new keys), tools/dogfood.py spawns a supervised server subprocess; dependency: none, stdlib only; concurrency: dogfood uses a temp sandbox db and a free port; state: dogfood writes only .aikit/dogfood_last_run.log and must leave the tracked tree clean
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the pdf guard and the stats block, fingerprint the tracked tree before and after the dogfood run, supervise every subprocess with full-tree teardown, keep the dogfood report under 15 lines with full log on disk

checkpoints.description: [5/5] Delivered the validation and adoption pass: .pdf ingestion now fails with the pdftotext/BibTeX recipe before reading binary bytes (2 tests), tools/dogfood.py drives the real CLI golden path plus the live studio server over HTTP with a chaos track and tracked-tree fingerprint (25/25 steps, exit 0), README gets the PDF recipes, the dogfood gate entries and the MCP agent integration guide, and stats gains an evidence health block (claims per paper, answered/open/abandoned, linked questions, coverage gaps, contested, links) rendered by the CLI and served by MCP/studio; .aikit/*.log is gitignored; 195 tests pass, 4/4 gates pass, dogfood 25/25; checklists: passed; both this task and the earlier UI-guard task remain uncommitted pending user authorization
Task 'lattice-validation-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Plan: Research Studio Evidence Health and Graph Inspector integration - (1) add Evidence Health metrics in header stats bar and outline drawer, (2) add Graph Node Inspector card displaying full quote/provenance on node selection, (3) verify with AIKit UI guard and Phase 4 gates

impact_assessment.why: the Research Studio lacked live visual feedback for the evidence health block (gaps and contested counts) added in ADR-021, and clicking graph nodes lacked an immediate detailed provenance inspector card
impact_assessment.benefits: researchers see evidence health and coverage gaps in real time across the stats bar and corpus outline drawer, and clicking any graph node instantly reveals its assertion, quote, and locator without leaving the graph tab
impact_assessment.risks: contract: surface bounded to lattice/web.py within 400 lines budget; dependency: none, stdlib only; concurrency: client-side DOM updates; state: no schema changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: re-run python aikit.py ui verify lattice, dogfood and all unittests; keep existing 116 inventory entries intact so no removals occur

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Delivered Research Studio Evidence Health and Graph Inspector: (1) added Gaps and Contested pills to header stats bar, (2) embedded Evidence Health metrics breakdown in Corpus Outline drawer, (3) added #graph-node-detail card under #svg-container with instant provenance inspection on node click, (4) verified through AIKit UI guard contract (0 strikes, 0 lost inventory entries), passing all 195 unit tests and 25/25 dogfood steps; ADR-022 recorded. checklists: passed.
Task 'lattice-studio-evidence-v1' completed successfully.

[1/4] Plan: multi-format graph export and NeuroCore article sync - (1) failing-first tests for GraphML and Cytoscape exports and sync_article_from_neurocore, (2) implement graphml/cytoscape in snapshots.py and cli.py, (3) implement sync_article_from_neurocore in api.py and client.py, (4) ADR-023, README, and Phase 4 gates

impact_assessment.why: Researchers need standard graph interchange formats (GraphML for Gephi/Cytoscape/NetworkX and Cytoscape JSON) and NeuroCore needs a field-mapped synchronization entry point fulfilling ADR-012
impact_assessment.benefits: The evidence graph can be opened in Gephi and Cytoscape with typed nodes and relations, and NeuroCore agents can sync structured research articles and findings into Lattice with one call
impact_assessment.risks: contract: export gains graphml and cytoscape formats; dependency: stdlib only (xml.etree.ElementTree and json); concurrency: unchanged atomic file writes; state: no database schema changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: assert XML well-formedness and schema attributes in tests, validate Cytoscape JSON elements shape, and ensure all existing snapshot JSONL tests pass unchanged

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Delivered multi-format graph export and NeuroCore article sync: (1) export_graphml_string/file for Gephi/Cytoscape XML, (2) export_cytoscape_data/file for web graphs, (3) CLI export auto-detects and accepts --format graphml|cytoscape, (4) sync_article_from_neurocore in ingest/api normalizes articles and extracts quote-backed claims, (5) LatticeClient methods and MCP format support; ADR-023; checklists: passed; 199 tests, 4/4 gates, dogfood 25/25.
